## 1.1 Bring in data for a Singular File

-   **What:** The code below sets file path and brings in the student and transcript data that you will need to select your snapshot of students.

-   **Project Team Action:** Replace folder path with the folder path where your files are and replace specific files names as necessary.

```{r, warning = F, message = F}

raw_data_folder_path_cohort <- "District Partners/Nashville/Nashville - HS Pathways - 2025/1. Data & Analysis - Secure/Transcript Analysis"

raw_data_folder_path_pathway_catalog <- "District Partners/Nashville/Nashville - HS Pathways - 2025/1. Data & Analysis - Secure/Sources of Truth"

raw_data_folder_path_2 <- "District Partners/Nashville/Nashville - HS Pathways - 2025/1. Data & Analysis - Secure/Pathway-Level Evaluation"

#base files
stu_transcript_rollup <- ers_read_sharepoint(folder_path = raw_data_folder_path_cohort,
                   file_name_with_extension = "MNPS_Draft_Student_Cohort.csv",
  drive_name = "client_work_drive")

pathway_catalog <- ers_read_sharepoint(folder_path = raw_data_folder_path_pathway_catalog,,
                   file_name_with_extension = "Pathway Coding by Course - 9.10.2025.xlsx",
  drive_name = "client_work_drive")

traditional_course_catalog <- ers_read_sharepoint(folder_path = raw_data_folder_path_cohort,,
                   file_name_with_extension = "03_course_coding_24-25 - CODED 10.24.xlsx",
  drive_name = "client_work_drive")


#Pathways to include and Pathway/Cluster crosswalk
pathways_to_include <- ers_read_sharepoint(folder_path = raw_data_folder_path_pathway_catalog,
                   file_name_with_extension = "Pathway Offerings 24-25 & 25-26.xlsx",
  drive_name = "client_work_drive")


#Percent completer data
percent_completers <- ers_read_sharepoint(folder_path = raw_data_folder_path_pathway_catalog,
  file_name_with_extension = "2024-25 Pathway Completers.xlsx",
  drive_name = "client_work_drive")

#H3 Data
h_3_data <- ers_read_sharepoint(folder_path = raw_data_folder_path_2,
  file_name_with_extension = "1A_Pathway-Level Evaluation.xlsx",
  sheet_name = "Pathway Evaluation - Heat Map",
  skip_rows = 1,
  drive_name = "client_work_drive")



#Set processed path now
processed_data_folder_path <-  "District Partners/Nashville/Nashville - HS Pathways - 2025/1. Data & Analysis - Secure/Transcript Analysis/Analysis_Exports_From_R"


```

###1.2 MNPS- Pre Analysis Pathway and Course Catalog Appending -
**What:** Because we took a little bit of a different path for MNPS, I am going to need to append the pathway course data and the traditional course catalog here before we move on.

####A. Filter to just Cohort Students

```{r}
#check distinct students before applying filters
stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  summarize(count_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id)) %>%
  print()


#Filter to students who met the duration criteria, or were present in the district for 75% of the year for each year of your analysis
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
filter(H_cohort_duration_include == "include")

#Filter to students who met the persistence criteria, or progressed traditionally from 9th to 12th grade in each of the years of your analysis
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
filter(H_cohort_progression_include == "include")

#Count the new unique number of students, which should now be your cohort number
stu_transcript_rollup %>%
summarize(count_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id)) %>%
print()

#Check the count by year, which should be the same number in each year
stu_transcript_rollup %>%
group_by(D_year) %>%
summarize(count_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id)) %>%
ungroup() %>%
print()

#great, all set there.

#Drop the helper columns for location, duration, and persistence
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
select(-starts_with("H_stay_duration"),
         -starts_with("H_stu_progression"),
         -starts_with("duration_"))

#and clean up some other column names. Remove the following column names-
columns_to_remove <- c("D_stu_grade_level_transcript", "D_stu_grade_level_demo", "M_days_enrolled", "C_9th_in_22", "M_years_enrolled", "grade_mismatch", "H_cohort_duration_include", "school_included", "H_cohort_progression_include") 
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
select(-all_of(columns_to_remove))


#rename in home_school_year James Lawson High School to James Lawson High
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  mutate(C_year_home_school = ifelse(C_year_home_school == "James Lawson High School", "James Lawson High", C_year_home_school))


#and rename any values of "Hillwood High" to "James Lawson High" as well
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  mutate(C_year_home_school = ifelse(C_year_home_school == "Hillwood High", "James Lawson High", C_year_home_school))



```

####B. Create Pure Cohort Flag
```{r}
#2306

# Step 1: Create a student-level flag for pure cohort
pure_students <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarise(
    transferred_any = any(C_transferred_across_years_flag == "Y" | 
                          C_transfered_within_year_flag == "Y"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(C_pure_cohort = ifelse(transferred_any, "N", "Y")) %>%
  select(D_stu_id, C_pure_cohort)

# Step 2: Join that flag back to all rows of stu_transcript_rollup
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  select(-any_of("C_pure_cohort")) %>%  # drop old version if it exists
  left_join(pure_students, by = "D_stu_id")

# Step 3: Count pure cohort students to make sure it worked
stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  filter(C_pure_cohort == "Y") %>%
  summarise(count_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id)) %>%
  print()

#and count students with the flag to make sure it worked
stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  filter(C_pure_cohort == "Y") %>%
  summarize(count_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id)) %>%
  print()

#1599


#how many students are removed from each distinct flag?
stu_transcript_rollup %>% 
  filter(C_transferred_across_years_flag == "Y") %>% 
  summarize(count_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id)) %>%
  print()

#459

stu_transcript_rollup %>% 
  filter(C_transfered_within_year_flag == "Y") %>% 
  summarize(count_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id)) %>%
  print()

#528

# Step 1: Summarize exclusion flags at the student level
exclusion_reasons <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarise(
    transferred_across = any(C_transferred_across_years_flag == "Y"),
    transferred_within = any(C_transfered_within_year_flag == "Y"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    exclusion_reason = case_when(
      transferred_across & transferred_within ~ "Both: Across & Within Year",
      transferred_across & !transferred_within ~ "Across Years Only",
      !transferred_across & transferred_within ~ "Within Year Only",
      TRUE ~ "Pure Cohort"   # fallback, should align with your C_pure_cohort == "Y"
    )
  )

# Step 2: Count students by reason
exclusion_counts <- exclusion_reasons %>%
  group_by(exclusion_reason) %>%
  summarise(num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id), .groups = "drop")

print(exclusion_counts)



```


####C. Update Location Codes

```{r}
#09/12 realizing that there was an issue with the location ID coming all the way down, so addressing it here in the hopes that it fixes the downstream problems

stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  mutate(
    # Reassign D_location_id based on C_four_year_home_school
    D_location_id = case_when(
      C_four_year_home_school == "Antioch High School"       ~ 110,
      C_four_year_home_school == "Cane Ridge High School"    ~ 182,
      C_four_year_home_school == "Glencliff High School"     ~ 325,
      C_four_year_home_school == "Hillsboro High"            ~ 435,
      C_four_year_home_school == "Hunters Lane High"        ~ 452,
      C_four_year_home_school == "James Lawson High School"  ~ 445,
      C_four_year_home_school == "John Overton High"         ~ 615,
      C_four_year_home_school == "McGavock High"            ~ 532,
      C_four_year_home_school == "PearlCohn High"           ~ 632,
      C_four_year_home_school == "Stratford"                ~ 705,
      C_four_year_home_school == "Whites Creek High School"             ~ 787,
      C_four_year_home_school == "Maplewood High"           ~ 550,  # Added Maplewood High,
      TRUE ~ as.numeric(D_location_id)  # keep original for all others
    )
  )

#Look at distinct combinations of C_year_home_school and C_year_home_school_id
stu_transcript_rollup %>% 
  distinct(C_four_year_home_school, D_location_id) %>%
  print()



#UPDATE PATCH- Create year home_school field
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  mutate(
    C_year_home_school_id = case_when(
      C_year_home_school == "Antioch High School"       ~ 110,
      C_year_home_school == "Cane Ridge High School"    ~ 182,
      C_year_home_school == "Glencliff High School"     ~ 325,
      C_year_home_school == "Hillsboro High"            ~ 435,
      C_year_home_school == "Hunters Lane High"         ~ 452,
      C_year_home_school == "James Lawson High School"  ~ 445,
      C_year_home_school == "John Overton High"         ~ 615,
      C_year_home_school == "McGavock High"             ~ 532,
      C_year_home_school == "PearlCohn High"            ~ 632,
      C_year_home_school == "Stratford"                 ~ 705,
      C_year_home_school == "Whites Creek High School"  ~ 787,
      C_year_home_school == "Maplewood High"          ~ 550,  # Added Maplewood High,
      C_year_home_school == "Hillwood High"           ~445,
      C_year_home_school == "James Lawson High"       ~445,
      TRUE ~ 000   # everything else gets 000
    )
  )

#Look at distinct combinations of C_year_home_school and C_year_home_school_id
stu_transcript_rollup %>% 
  distinct(C_year_home_school, C_year_home_school_id) %>%
  print()

#And fix the student race/ethnicity dupe thing I discovered later on
# 1️⃣ Identify the students with multiple race values
multi_race_students <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  distinct(D_stu_id, D_stu_race) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(num_races = n_distinct(D_stu_race), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(num_races > 1)

# 2️⃣ Create a lookup table: randomly select one race per student
set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility
race_lookup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  filter(D_stu_id %in% multi_race_students$D_stu_id) %>%
  distinct(D_stu_id, D_stu_race) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 1) %>%   # randomly pick one race
  ungroup()

# 3️⃣ Apply it to the original data
stu_transcript_rollup_clean <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  left_join(race_lookup, by = "D_stu_id", suffix = c("", "_new")) %>%
  mutate(
    D_stu_race = ifelse(D_stu_id %in% multi_race_students$D_stu_id, D_stu_race_new, D_stu_race)
  ) %>%
  select(-D_stu_race_new)

# 4️⃣ Optional check: ensure no student has multiple races
stu_transcript_rollup_clean %>%
  distinct(D_stu_id, D_stu_race) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(num_races = n_distinct(D_stu_race), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(num_races > 1)  # should return 0 rows


```

####D. Preparing the pathways coding

```{r}
# show all catalog columns that start with "pathway_"
pathway_columns <- names(pathway_catalog)[str_detect(names(pathway_catalog), "^pathway_\\d+_")]
pathway_columns

#check distinct number of courses (should not change) before pivot longer
pathway_catalog %>%
  summarize(count_courses = n_distinct(D_course_id)) %>%
  print()

#pivot longer
pathway_catalog_long <- pathway_catalog %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^pathway_\\d+_"),
    names_to = c("pathway_num", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "pathway_(\\d+)_(.*)"
  ) %>%
  # the pivot will create columns like: pathway, cluster, level, etc.
  filter(!is.na(pathway) & pathway != "") %>%   # keep only real pathway slots
  mutate(pathway_num = as.integer(pathway_num)) %>%
  distinct()

#check distinct number of courses (should not have changed) after pivot longer
pathway_catalog_long %>%
  summarize(count_courses = n_distinct(D_course_id)) %>%
  print()

#Clean up the course names
pathway_catalog_long <- pathway_catalog_long %>%
  mutate(C_course_id_clean = str_replace(D_course_id, "([[:punct:]]?\\s*)?(S1|S2)\\s*$", ""))

#and remove the columns that we won't need from pathways
pathway_catalog_long <- pathway_catalog_long %>%
  select(-C_course_EPSO_type, -C_course_subject_area)

#Now, lets look at overlap in distinct values of "Pathway" compared to distinct values of C_school_pathway_name in pathways to include. What pathways from the pathawy_catalog_long are listed there, which are not?
# Distinct pathway names in each
catalog_paths <- pathway_catalog_long %>%
  distinct(pathway)

include_paths <- pathways_to_include %>%
  distinct(C_school_pathway_name)

# Find what's in catalog but not in include list
catalog_not_in_include <- catalog_paths %>%
  anti_join(include_paths, by = c("pathway" = "C_school_pathway_name"))

catalog_not_in_include

```

####E. Append in the traditional Catalog

```{r}
# Step 1. Clean cohort course IDs (strip "S1"/"S2" if present)
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  mutate(D_course_id_cleaned = str_replace(D_course_id, "([[:punct:]]?\\s*)?(S1|S2)\\s*$", ""))

# Step 2. Get distinct IDs from both sources
course_catalog_ids <- unique(traditional_course_catalog$C_course_id_clean)
cohort_ids <- unique(stu_transcript_rollup$D_course_id_cleaned)

# Step 3. Compare
ids_in_both       <- intersect(cohort_ids, course_catalog_ids)
ids_only_catalog  <- setdiff(course_catalog_ids, cohort_ids)
ids_only_cohort <- setdiff(cohort_ids, course_catalog_ids)

# Step 4. Counts
cat("Total unique IDs in catalog:", length(course_catalog_ids), "\n")
cat("Total unique IDs in cohort:", length(cohort_ids), "\n")
cat("IDs present in BOTH:", length(ids_in_both), "\n")
cat("IDs only in catalog:", length(ids_only_catalog), "\n")
cat("IDs only in cohort:", length(ids_only_cohort), "\n")

#okay great, then rename D_course_id_cleaned to C_course_id_clean to match the catalog
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>% 
  rename(C_course_id_clean = D_course_id_cleaned)

#and drop course_name, D_course_id from the transcript data, since we will be bringing in the catalog course name and we have the cleaned IDs to match off of
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  select(-D_course_name, -D_course_id)


#check number of rows before the join
nrow_before_join <- nrow(stu_transcript_rollup) %>% 
  print()


#Okay, so because the catalog had multiple duplicate rows per course ID, we need to filter to just distinct rows by course ID before we join to avoid creating duplicate rows of enrollment
traditional_course_catalog <- traditional_course_catalog %>%
  distinct(C_course_id_clean, .keep_all = TRUE)

#now join in the traditional course catalog to the cohort data
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  left_join(traditional_course_catalog, by = "C_course_id_clean")

# Check how many unmatched courses (catalog NAs)
na_check <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  filter(is.na(C_course_name_clean)) %>%         # or any key column from catalog
  distinct(C_course_name_clean)
message("Number of unmatched course IDs: ", nrow(na_check))

#check rows after
nrow_after_join <- nrow(stu_transcript_rollup)

#great, and lets do some checks to make sure it worked. Note that the "Simon Added" courses won't have complete information that the other courses have, because we added them manually

#check distinct number of courses (should not change) after join (should be 833)
stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  summarize(count_courses = n_distinct(C_course_id_clean)) %>%
  print()

#lets drop D_course_id, D_course_name, and the "n" column we only need the cleaned names and codes and IDK what n is doing
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  select(-D_course_id, -D_course_name, -n)


#Okay great and lets just double check some students
student_dive_1 <- stu_transcript_rollup %>% 
  filter(D_stu_id == "190117730") %>% 
  print()

student_dive_2 <- stu_transcript_rollup %>% 
  filter(D_stu_id == "190137772") %>% 
  print()

student_dive_3 <- stu_transcript_rollup %>% 
  filter(D_stu_id == "190144192") %>% 
  print()

student_dive_4 <- stu_transcript_rollup %>% 
  filter(D_stu_id == "190145518") %>% 
  print()


#checking for things like-
  #looks like they took the right sorts of courses in the right years
  #credit counts still look normal
  #flags for courses look normal

#Student 1-
#So looks like they are tagged demographic wise as an SWD and ELL, and their course-taking reflects that. They have a few rows with NA values in grade/credits, but looking at the course-names it seems like these are specific SWD courses. Otherwise looks good!

#Student 2-
#great grades, also SWD, took some Dual Enrollment courses, looks good!

#Student 3-
#looks normal but also showing as a student with SWD, so want to quickly check the rate of that in cohort because the odds of selecting three students at random and having them all tagegd as a SWD feels low

#check distribution of SWD Flag
stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  group_by(D_stu_ell, D_stu_swd) %>% 
  summarize(count_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  print()

#okay

#Clean up name values in C_course_EPSO_type. Rename "Dual Credit / Dual Enrollment" to "Dual Credit/Dual Enrollment", and "Industry Cedential" to "Industry Credential"
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  mutate(C_course_EPSO_type = case_when(
    C_course_EPSO_type == "Dual Credit / Dual Enrollment" ~ "Dual Credit/Dual Enrollment",
    C_course_EPSO_type == "Industry Cedential" ~ "Industry Credential",
    TRUE ~ C_course_EPSO_type
  ))


```

####F. Creating Pathway Data-Frame

```{r}
#Okay first create a new-data frame
cohort_pathways <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  left_join(pathway_catalog_long, by = "C_course_id_clean") %>%
  # keep only rows that have pathway info
  filter(!is.na(pathway) & pathway != "")

#and it should be a one to many, that makes sense
#double check distinct students in that data-frame
cohort_pathways %>%
  summarize(count_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id)) %>%
  print()

# Assign pathway_id to cohort_pathways
cohort_pathways <- cohort_pathways %>%
  left_join(pathway_lookup, by = "pathway")

# Quick check to confirm assignment worked
check_assign <- cohort_pathways %>%
  select(pathway, pathway_id) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(pathway_id)


#rename "pathway_id" to "C_pathway_id" for consistency
cohort_pathways <- cohort_pathways %>%
  rename(C_pathway_id = pathway_id)

#okay yeah I think all the NAs are fine, because those are the superfluous rows we will exclude later

#Okay great, now we want to filter the cohort_pathways data-frame to just pathways we want to "include" based on our source of truth document

# build include/exclude
pathway_flags <- pathways_to_include %>%
  select(D_location_id, C_pathway_id, `C_school_pathway_include_flag_24-25`) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  rename(
    include_flag = `C_school_pathway_include_flag_24-25`
  )

#and lets make sure all of the fields are the same data-type
pathway_flags <- pathway_flags %>%
  mutate(
    D_location_id = as.integer(D_location_id),
    C_pathway_id = as.integer(C_pathway_id)
  )

#and in the cohort pathways data-frame
cohort_pathways <- cohort_pathways %>%
  mutate(
    C_year_home_school_id = as.integer(C_year_home_school_id),
    C_pathway_id = as.integer(C_pathway_id)
  )

# show keys with >1 row or with flags other than exactly "Include"
pathway_flags %>%
  group_by(D_location_id, C_pathway_id) %>%
  summarize(
    flags = paste(sort(unique(include_flag)), collapse = " | "),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n > 1 | flags != "Include") %>%
  arrange(D_location_id, C_pathway_id) %>%
  print(n = 500)

# merge flag
cohort_with_flags <- cohort_pathways %>%
  left_join(pathway_flags,
            by = c("C_year_home_school_id" = "D_location_id",
                   "C_pathway_id" = "C_pathway_id"))

# which pathways at which schools have exclude flag?
cohort_with_flags %>%
  filter(include_flag == "Exclude") %>%
  distinct(C_year_home_school, C_pathway_id, include_flag) %>%
  arrange(C_year_home_school, C_pathway_id) %>%
  print()

#check that no rows are NA
cohort_with_flags %>%
  filter(is.na(include_flag)) %>%
  distinct(C_year_home_school, C_pathway_id, include_flag) %>%
  arrange(C_year_home_school, C_pathway_id) %>%
  print()

# Exclude rows
cohort_pathways <- cohort_with_flags %>%
  filter(is.na(include_flag) | include_flag != "Exclude")

# check that student count should not change
cohort_pathways %>%
```

####J. Resolving cross pathway course enrollments using completer data
```{r}
#How many students in the cohort_aalnalysis_dataframe have more than one pathway for the same course id?
cross_pathway_students <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(C_pure_cohort == "Y", in_completer_data == TRUE, valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id, course_id) %>%
  summarize(
    distinct_pathways = n_distinct(pathway),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(distinct_pathways > 1) %>%
  distinct(D_stu_id) %>% 
  print()

#how many distinct student IDs in cross_pathway_students?
length(unique(cross_pathway_students$D_stu_id))

#okay 420. For those 420 students, how many of them have a pathway completion in ONE of the pathways that the course ID is a multiple for, but not the other(s)?
students_to_resolve <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(D_stu_id %in% cross_pathway_students$D_stu_id,
         C_pure_cohort == "Y",
         valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id, course_id) %>%
  summarize(
    distinct_pathways = n_distinct(pathway),
    pathways_completed = sum(C_pathway_completion == "YES", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(distinct_pathways > 1, pathways_completed == 1) %>%
  distinct(D_stu_id) %>%
  arrange(D_stu_id)

#Could I get a data-frame that shows the courses of these students that are causing these issues (so course ID and name) and the count of distinct students for whom that course is part of a cross-pathway sequence?
courses_causing_issues <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(D_stu_id %in% cross_pathway_students$D_stu_id,
         C_pure_cohort == "Y",
         valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id, course_id, C_course_name_clean) %>%
  summarize(
    distinct_pathways = n_distinct(pathway),
    pathways_completed = sum(C_pathway_completion == "YES", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(distinct_pathways > 1) %>%  # <- keep all cross-pathway students
  group_by(course_id, C_course_name_clean) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),

  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(num_students), course_id) %>% 
  print()
```

####K. Creating a non-IC EPSO field
```{r}
#what are all the possible values for C_course_EPSO_type?
stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  distinct(C_course_EPSO_type) %>%
  arrange(C_course_EPSO_type) %>%
  print()


#Post team meeting on 10/9, we have decided to remove ICs from counting toward EPSO. So we need to create a new column in both stu_transcript_rollup AND cohort_analysis_dataframe that groups by C_Course_EPSO_type and creates a new field called C_course_EPSO_no_IC that is TRUE for "Advanced Placement", "Cambridge AICE", "Dual Credit/Dual Enrollment", and FALSE for "Not EPSO" and "Industry Credential", and NA for "None" and NA for any other values
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  mutate(C_course_EPSO_no_IC = case_when(
    C_course_EPSO_type %in% c("Advanced Placement", "Cambridge", "Dual Credit/Dual Enrollment", "International Baccalaureate") ~ TRUE,
    C_course_EPSO_type %in% c("Not EPSO", "Industry Credential") ~ FALSE,
    C_course_EPSO_type %in% c("None") | is.na(C_course_EPSO_type) ~ NA,
    TRUE ~ NA  # catch any other unexpected values
  ))

cohort_analysis_dataframe <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  mutate(C_course_EPSO_no_IC = case_when(
    C_course_EPSO_type %in% c("Advanced Placement", "Cambridge", "Dual Credit/Dual Enrollment", "International Baccalaureate") ~ TRUE,
    C_course_EPSO_type %in% c("Not EPSO", "Industry Credential") ~ FALSE,
    C_course_EPSO_type %in% c("None") | is.na(C_course_EPSO_type) ~ NA,
    TRUE ~ NA  # catch any other unexpected values
  ))






```

```{r}
#grouping by pathway, how many students ever failed a course in a pathway
students_failed_pathway <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(C_pure_cohort == "Y", valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  # Step 1: Flag if student ever failed in each pathway
  group_by(D_stu_id, pathway) %>%
  summarize(
    ever_failed = any(C_course_failed == "Failed"),  # TRUE if student ever failed
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Step 2: Summarize at pathway level
  group_by(pathway) %>%
  summarize(
    total_students   = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    students_failed  = sum(ever_failed),
    students_no_fail = sum(!ever_failed),
    pct_failed       = students_failed / total_students,
    pct_no_fail      = students_no_fail / total_students,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Step 3: Pivot longer for clean display (rows = measure, cols = pathway)
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(total_students, students_failed, students_no_fail,
             pct_failed, pct_no_fail),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = pathway,
    values_from = value
  )
```

```{r}
#Using cohort_analysis_dataframe and valid combos, what is the average (median) number of credits (D_creds_possible) that students are attempting each year, overall?

    median_credits = median(total_credits, na.rm = TRUE),
```

```{r}
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE, !is.na(C_course_EPSO_type), C_course_EPSO_type != "Not EPSO") %>%
  group_by(pathway, C_year_home_school, C_course_EPSO_type, D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    total_epsos = sum(D_creds_earn, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(pathway, C_year_home_school, C_course_EPSO_type) %>%
  summarize(
    median_epsos = median(total_epsos),
    mean_epsos   = mean(total_epsos),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = C_year_home_school,
    values_from = c(median_epsos, mean_epsos)
  ) %>%
  arrange(pathway, C_course_EPSO_type) %>%
  print()

#Testing a hypothesis I have about course segregation
most_segregated_courses <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  group_by(C_course_name_clean, D_stu_race) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    .groups = "drop_last"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    total_students = sum(num_students),
    pct_of_course = num_students / total_students * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(C_course_name_clean) %>%
  filter(total_students >= 20) %>%  # only courses with 20+ total students
  summarize(
    total_students = first(total_students),
    dominant_race = D_stu_race[which.max(pct_of_course)],
    dominant_pct = max(pct_of_course)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_students), desc(dominant_pct)) %>%   # large + segregated at top
  print()

#Of students who complete any pathway, how many take a pathway course outside of the pathway that they completed?
completers_outside_pathway <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(in_completer_data == TRUE, valid_combo == TRUE, C_pure_cohort == "Y") %>%
  # 1️⃣ Identify each student's completed pathways
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    completed_pathways = list(unique(pathway[C_pathway_completion == "YES"])),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # 2️⃣ Join back to all their course enrollments
  left_join(
    cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
      filter(valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
      select(D_stu_id, pathway, course_id, C_course_name_clean),
    by = "D_stu_id"
  ) %>%
  # 3️⃣ Flag if the course is outside of their completed pathways
  mutate(
    took_outside_pathway_course = !pathway %in% unlist(completed_pathways)
  ) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    total_completers = n(),  # for info, could also just count unique students later
    completers_with_outside_course = any(took_outside_pathway_course, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  summarize(
    total_completers = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    completers_with_outside_course = sum(completers_with_outside_course),
    pct_with_outside_course = completers_with_outside_course / total_completers,
    pct_label = paste0(round(pct_with_outside_course * 100, 1), "%")
  ) %>%
  print()

#and then same thing but for students who did not complete 
non_completers_outside <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(in_completer_data == TRUE, valid_combo == TRUE, C_pure_cohort == "Y") %>%
  # 1️⃣ Identify pathways where student explicitly has "NO"
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    no_pathways = list(unique(pathway[C_pathway_completion == "NO"])),
    has_completed_any = any(C_pathway_completion == "YES"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!has_completed_any) %>%  # only students who did NOT complete any pathway
  # 2️⃣ Join back to all their enrollments
  left_join(
    cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
      filter(valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
      select(D_stu_id, pathway, course_id, C_course_name_clean),
    by = "D_stu_id"
  ) %>%
  # 3️⃣ Flag if the course is outside of their "NO" pathways
  mutate(
    took_outside_pathway_course = !pathway %in% unlist(no_pathways)
  ) %>%
  # 4️⃣ Summarize per student
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    took_outside_pathway_course = any(took_outside_pathway_course, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # 5️⃣ Summarize overall

#Similar to how I got a 100% breakdown of EPSO course taking by type at each school, I want to get a 100% breakdown of pathway enrollment by pathway and D_stu_race. So for each pathway, what % of each D_stu_race catagory makes up the students enrolled in that pathway?
pathway_enrollment_by_race <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE, in_completer_data == TRUE) %>%
  # Count unique students per pathway × race
  group_by(pathway, D_stu_race) %>%
  summarize(students_in_race = n_distinct(D_stu_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Get total students per pathway for denominator
  group_by(pathway) %>%
  mutate(
    total_students_pathway = sum(students_in_race),
    pct_of_pathway = students_in_race / total_students_pathway
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(D_stu_race, pathway, pct_of_pathway) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = pathway,
    values_from = pct_of_pathway,
    values_fill = 0  # fill 0 if a race has no students in a pathway
  ) %>%
  arrange(D_stu_race) %>% 
  print()
```

```{r}
school_pathway_summary <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  
  # summarize completion at student level
  group_by(pathway, C_year_home_school, D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    is_completer = any(C_pathway_completion == "YES", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop_last"
  ) %>%
  
  # summarize at school–pathway level
  summarize(
    total_students = n(),
    num_completers = sum(is_completer),
    pct_completers = num_completers / total_students,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # add EPSO course counts at school–pathway level
  left_join(
    cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
      filter(valid_combo == TRUE, C_course_EPSO_no_IC == TRUE) %>%
      group_by(pathway, C_year_home_school) %>%
      summarize(num_epsos = n_distinct(course_id), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("pathway", "C_year_home_school")
  ) %>%
  
  # create combined label and clean up
  mutate(
    school_pathway = paste(C_year_home_school, pathway, sep = ", "),
    pct_completers = round(pct_completers * 100, 1)
  ) %>%
  select(school_pathway, pct_completers, num_epsos) %>%
  arrange(school_pathway)

#Failure analysis

#first create a new column "course_failed?" in cohort_analysis_dataframe where if creds_earn is 0 and creds_possible > 0, then course_failed? == YES, otherwise NO
cohort_analysis_dataframe <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  mutate(
    course_failed = if_else(D_creds_possible > 0 & D_creds_earn == 0, "YES", "NO")
  )

#then filter to Yes to check some examples
cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(course_failed == "YES") %>%
  select(D_stu_id, course_id, C_course_name_clean, D_creds_possible, D_creds_earn, D_stu_grade) %>%
  print(n = 20)

#Checking failure rates
failure_by_completion <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    C_pathway_completion = case_when(
      any(C_pathway_completion == "YES") ~ "YES",
      any(C_pathway_completion == "NO") ~ "NO",
      TRUE ~ "UNKNOWN"
    ),
    ever_failed_pathway_course = any(course_failed == "YES"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(C_pathway_completion) %>%
  summarize(
    total_students = n(),
    num_who_failed = sum(ever_failed_pathway_course),
    pct_who_failed = num_who_failed / total_students,
    pct_label = paste0(round(pct_who_failed * 100, 1), "%"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(factor(C_pathway_completion, levels = c("YES", "NO", "UNKNOWN"))) %>%
  print()

#wow okay super telling. For students who DID fail a pathway course ever, when did they fail, or what was the n size grouped by year?
failure_timing <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    C_pathway_completion = case_when(
      any(C_pathway_completion == "YES") ~ "YES",
      any(C_pathway_completion == "NO") ~ "NO",
      TRUE ~ "UNKNOWN"
    ),
    failure_years = list(unique(D_year[course_failed == "YES"])),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  unnest(failure_years) %>%
  group_by(C_pathway_completion, failure_years) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(C_pathway_completion, failure_years) %>%
  print()


#Of students who failed a pathway course, how many were NOT pure cohort, or transfered either within or across years?
failure_by_transfer_status <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  
  # collapse to one row per student
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    ever_failed_pathway_course = if_else(any(course_failed == "YES", na.rm = TRUE), "YES", "NO"),
    C_pure_cohort = first(C_pure_cohort),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # summarize counts by pure cohort × failure status
  group_by(C_pure_cohort, ever_failed_pathway_course) %>%
  summarize(
    total_students = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(C_pure_cohort, ever_failed_pathway_course)

print(failure_by_transfer_status)


failure_completion_density <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  
  # Collapse to one row per student
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    num_failed_courses = sum(course_failed == "YES", na.rm = TRUE),
    completed_pathway = case_when(
      any(C_pathway_completion == "YES", na.rm = TRUE) ~ TRUE,
      all(C_pathway_completion == "NO" | is.na(C_pathway_completion)) ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ NA  # this handles students with mixed or unknown status
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Only include students with known completion status
  filter(!is.na(completed_pathway)) %>%
  
  # Summarize by number of failed courses (including 0)
  group_by(num_failed_courses) %>%
  summarize(
    n_students_completed = sum(completed_pathway),
    total_students = n(),
    pct_total = round((n_students_completed / total_students) * 100, 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(num_failed_courses)

print(failure_completion_density)
```

```{r}
#Can we do a table, district wide (all schools) using cohort analysis data-frame that shows the total number of EPSOs possible in a pathway (all schools) and then shows the median number of EPSOs that students in that pathway earn?
epsos_student_by_pathway <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE, C_course_EPSO_no_IC == TRUE) %>%

  summarize(
    n_epsos_attempted = n_distinct(course_id),

  )

# Summarize by pathway

  group_by(pathway) %>%
  summarize(
    median_epsos_attempted = median(n_epsos_attempted),
    mean_epsos_attempted = mean(n_epsos_attempted),
    median_epsos_earned = median(n_epsos_earned),
    mean_epsos_earned = mean(n_epsos_earned),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

    cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
      filter(valid_combo == TRUE, C_course_EPSO_no_IC == TRUE) %>%
      group_by(pathway) %>%
      summarize(total_epsos_possible = n_distinct(course_id), .groups = "drop"),

  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_epsos_possible))

#lets go about this another way. Using stu_transcript_rollup, can we create a new column called "failed_core" that is yes if C_course_failed and C_course_subject_type is one of Math, ELA, Science, Social Studies?
stu_transcript_rollup <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  mutate(
    failed_core = case_when(
      C_course_failed == "Failed" & C_course_subject_area %in% c("Math", "ELA", "Science", "Social Studies") ~ "YES",
      TRUE ~ "NO"
    )
  )


#What is the core course failure rate by school, or the percentage of students in each school who had ANY failed_core == "YES"?
core_failure_rate_by_school <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  # Keep only AON school rows
  filter(is_AON_school == "YES") %>%
  # Flag if a student ever failed a core course
  group_by(C_year_home_school, D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    ever_failed_core = if_else(any(failed_core == "YES", na.rm = TRUE), "YES", "NO"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Compute school-level stats
  group_by(C_year_home_school) %>%
  summarize(
    total_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    num_failed_core = sum(ever_failed_core == "YES"),
    pct_failed_core = num_failed_core / total_students,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_failed_core)) %>%
  print()


#Using stu_transcript_rollup, can we get the % of students by demographic group in each C_year_home_school (that is AON) that ever took an EPSO course?
epsos_by_demographic_and_school <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  # Keep only AON schools
  filter(is_AON_school == "YES") %>%
  
  # Flag if a student ever took an EPSO course
  group_by(C_year_home_school, D_stu_id, D_stu_race) %>% 
  summarize(
    ever_took_EPSO = if_else(any(C_course_EPSO_no_IC == TRUE, na.rm = TRUE), "YES", "NO"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Compute school-year x race stats and keep only pct
  group_by(C_year_home_school, D_stu_race) %>% 
  summarize(
    pct_took_EPSO = mean(ever_took_EPSO == "YES"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Pivot wider so school-years become columns
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = C_year_home_school,
    values_from = pct_took_EPSO
  )

#Okay, for all pathways that offer at least one EPSO, what is the percentage of students who earn at least 1 EPSO in those pathways?
epsos_earned_by_pathway <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE, C_course_EPSO_no_IC == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(pathway, D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    n_epsos_earned = n_distinct(course_id[C_course_failed == "Not Failed"]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(pathway) %>%
  summarize(
    total_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    num_earned_at_least_one = sum(n_epsos_earned >= 1),
    pct_earned_at_least_one = num_earned_at_least_one / total_students,
    pct_label = paste0(round(pct_earned_at_least_one * 100, 1), "%"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_earned_at_least_one)) %>%
  print()

    overall_pct_earned_at_least_one = total_earned_at_least_one / total_students,
    pct_label = paste0(round(overall_pct_earned_at_least_one * 100, 1), "%")
  ) %>%
  print()

    # Keep only grades 10–12 and valid combos
  filter(C_eoy_grade %in% c(10, 11, 12), valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  # Count distinct courses per student per pathway
  group_by(D_stu_id, pathway) %>%
  summarize(
    num_pathway_courses_taken = n_distinct(course_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Collapse to student-level: get the maximum number of courses they took in any pathway
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    max_courses_in_any_pathway = max(num_pathway_courses_taken, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Create MECE bucket
  mutate(
    course_bucket = case_when(
      max_courses_in_any_pathway > 3 ~ "More than 3 courses",
      max_courses_in_any_pathway <= 3 ~ "3 or fewer courses"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Count **students once** per bucket
  group_by(course_bucket) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(course_bucket) %>%
  print()

#I thought I had done this but I guess not, can we do a big table using cohort_analysis_data-frame that summarizes the number of credits (D_creds_possible) by pathway that students are attempting each year? So the rows would be pathways, the columns would be years (C_eoy_grade), and the values would be the average of D_creds_possible for students in that pathway at that school that year.
credits_by_pathway_and_year <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(pathway, C_eoy_grade, D_stu_id) %>%     # first group by student
  summarize(
    total_credits = sum(D_creds_possible, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(pathway, C_eoy_grade) %>%              # now summarize across students
  summarize(
    avg_credits_attempted = median(total_credits, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = C_eoy_grade,
    values_from = avg_credits_attempted,
    names_prefix = "Grade_"
  ) %>%
  arrange(pathway) %>%
  print()

#okay and then
students_credit_buckets_total <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  # Keep only grades 10–12 and valid combos
  filter(C_eoy_grade %in% c(10, 11, 12), valid_combo == TRUE) %>%
  # Sum credits per student across all courses in each pathway
  group_by(D_stu_id, pathway) %>%
  summarize(
    total_credits = sum(D_creds_possible, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Bucket students per pathway
  mutate(
    credit_bucket = case_when(
      total_credits < 3 ~ "Fewer than 3 credits",
      total_credits == 3 ~ "Exactly 3 credits",
      total_credits > 3 ~ "More than 3 credits"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Count **distinct students across all pathways**, ensuring MECE
  group_by(D_stu_id, credit_bucket) %>%
  slice_max(total_credits, n = 1) %>%  # take the max bucket if student is in multiple pathways
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(credit_bucket) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(credit_bucket) %>%
  print()
```

```{r}
#Okay moving on- create a new dataframe from out_of_zone_enrollment that just filters to "Active" Status students

#add glencliff

glencliff <- ers_read_sharepoint(folder_path = zone_enrollement_data_folder_path,
  file_name_with_extension = "Glencliff.xlsx",
  drive_name = "client_work_drive",
  skip_rows = 9)

glencliff <- glencliff %>%
  mutate(school_attended = "Glencliff High School")

#remove duplicate rows
glencliff <- glencliff %>%
  distinct(ID, school_attended, .keep_all = TRUE)

#remove rows we don't need
glencliff <- glencliff %>%
  select(ID, school_attended, Grade, Gen., Ethn., SWD, ED, ELL, Status, `Out of Zone`, `Zoned School`, Homeless)

#Mask ID column by renaming to D_stu_id and multiplying it by 1.2, adding a random letter (group by student_id)
glencliff <- glencliff %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  mutate(D_stu_id = as.character(as.numeric(ID) * 1.2 + sample(1000:9999, n(), replace = TRUE))) %>%
  select(-ID)

#remove the "ID" column fom Glencliff
glencliff <- glencliff %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-ID)

#make sure all of the column types in glencliff match out_of_zone_active_students
glencliff <- glencliff %>%
  mutate(
    Grade = as.character(Grade),
    Gen. = as.character(Gen.),
    Ethn. = as.character(Ethn.),
    SWD = as.character(SWD),
    ED = as.character(ED),
    ELL = as.character(ELL),
    Status = as.character(Status),
    `Out of Zone` = as.character(`Out of Zone`),
    `Zoned School` = as.character(`Zoned School`),
    Homeless = as.character(Homeless),
    school_attended = as.character(school_attended),
    D_stu_id = as.character(D_stu_id)
  )

out_of_zone_active_students <- out_of_zone_active_students %>%
  mutate(
    Grade = as.character(Grade),
    Gen. = as.character(Gen.),
    Ethn. = as.character(Ethn.),
    SWD = as.character(SWD),
    ED = as.character(ED),
    ELL = as.character(ELL),
    Status = as.character(Status),
    `Out of Zone` = as.character(`Out of Zone`),
    `Zoned School` = as.character(`Zoned School`),
    Homeless = as.character(Homeless),
    school_attended = as.character(school_attended),
    D_stu_id = as.character(D_stu_id)
  )


#Add the glencliff rows to out_of_zone_active_students
```

```{r}
#We have this question about if students are more or less likley to fail certain kinds of pathway EPSOs (AP vs DE vs IB). So using cohort_analysis_dataframe, can we filter to EPSOs (including ICs!) and count total enrollments (rows) and then count total enollments failed (C_course_failed = "Failed), then calculate percent failed by C_course_EPSO_type (AP, DE, IB)
epsos_failed_by_type <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(C_course_EPSO == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(C_course_EPSO_type) %>%
  summarize(
    total_enrollments = n(),
    total_failed = sum(C_course_failed == "Failed", na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_failed = total_failed / total_enrollments,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(C_course_EPSO_type) %>%
  print()

#what if instead of C_failed we used D_stu_grade of 60 or below
epsos_failed_by_type_grade <- cohort_analysis_dataframe %>%
  filter(C_course_EPSO == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(C_course_EPSO_type) %>%
  summarize(
    total_enrollments = n(),
    total_failed = sum(D_stu_grade <= 60, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_failed = total_failed / total_enrollments,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(C_course_EPSO_type) %>%
  print()

#how many failed both semesters of a 9th, 10th, and 11th grade class
students_failed_both_terms_any_class_9th_10th_11th <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  filter(C_eoy_grade %in% c(9, 10, 11)) %>%
  
  # keep grade before summarizing
  group_by(D_stu_id, C_course_id_clean, C_eoy_grade) %>%
  summarize(
    failed_both_terms = all(C_course_failed == "Failed"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # only keep courses where the student failed both terms
  filter(failed_both_terms == TRUE) %>%
  
  # now summarize at the student level
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    failed_9th = any(C_eoy_grade == 9),
    failed_10th = any(C_eoy_grade == 10),
    failed_11th = any(C_eoy_grade == 11),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # student must have failures in all three grades
  filter(failed_9th, failed_10th, failed_11th) %>%
  
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pull(num_students) %>%
  print()

  # keep grade before summarizing

  summarize(
    failed_both_terms = all(C_course_failed == "Failed"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # summarize at the student level
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    ever_failed_9th = any(C_eoy_grade == 9 & failed_both_terms == TRUE),
```

```{r}
#What can we understand about credit recovery? 
#Note from RT/MM Identifying credit recovery courses "Look for two of the same course IDs on the transcript, the first (failed one) counting for 0 credits and the second (recovery one) passed with a grade of exactly 60 (one year it was 70) and counting for 0.5 credits (one semester)"

#How many students have duplicate rows for the same Course ID and same semester (D_term) more than once?
duplicate_course_enrollments <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id, C_course_id_clean, C_eoy_grade, D_year, D_term) %>%
  summarize(
    enrollment_count = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(enrollment_count > 1) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    num_duplicate_enrollments = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

#Testing this
stu_transcript_rollup_credit_recovery <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  arrange(D_stu_id, C_course_id_clean, D_year, D_term) %>%  # ensure ordering
  group_by(D_stu_id, C_course_id_clean) %>%
  
  # Identify the failed attempt(s): same student + course + term where credits = 0
  mutate(
    failed_row = D_creds_earn == 0
  ) %>%
  
  # For each row, check if there was a *prior* failed attempt in the SAME TERM
  mutate(
    prior_failed_same_term = purrr::map_lgl(
      seq_len(n()),
      ~ any(
        failed_row[1:(.x - 1)] &
        D_term[1:(.x - 1)] == D_term[.x]
      )
    ),
    
    # Final credit recovery flag
    C_credit_recovery_course = case_when(
      prior_failed_same_term &
        D_stu_grade == 60 &
        D_creds_earn > 0 ~ "Y",
      TRUE ~ "N"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Step 3: Join WBL info to students

  left_join(wbl_courses_per_pathway, by = c("C_year_home_school", "pathway")) %>%
  # Pathways with no WBL courses get 0
  mutate(num_wbl_courses = replace_na(num_wbl_courses, 0)) %>%
  group_by(num_wbl_courses, C_pathway_completion) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),  # count unique students
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(num_wbl_courses, C_pathway_completion)

#Okay, lets see if I can do it this way, I want to make a big table that shows me the percentage of students by school who take EPSOs by certain course types. So first I want to filter stu_transcript_rollup to just 12th grade, and then I want to group by C_year_home_school where each unique value is a row, then I want one column that shows the total number of Math EPSOs that school offers, then the total number of students enrolled in any math EPSO at that school, and then the percentage of total students that represents (out of all distinct D_stu_id at that school). I want to do this for Math, Science, English, and Social Studies, so there should be 12 columns.
epsos_by_subject_area_and_school_12th_grade <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  filter(C_eoy_grade == 12, C_course_EPSO_no_IC == TRUE) %>%
  group_by(C_year_home_school, C_course_subject_area) %>%
  summarize(
    total_epsos_offered = n_distinct(C_course_name_clean),
    students_in_epsos = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = C_course_subject_area,
    values_from = c(total_epsos_offered, students_in_epsos),
    names_glue = "{C_course_subject_area}_{.value}"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    stu_transcript_rollup %>%
      filter(C_eoy_grade == 12) %>%
      group_by(C_year_home_school) %>%
      summarize(
        total_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "C_year_home_school"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_math_epsos = Math_students_in_epsos / total_students,
    pct_science_epsos = Science_students_in_epsos / total_students,
    pct_english_epsos = English_students_in_epsos / total_students,
    pct_social_studies_epsos = `Social Studies_students_in_epsos` / total_students
  ) %>%
  arrange(C_year_home_school) %>%
  print()
```

```{r}
#okay I need to re-do a big table that I KNOW I have done before- using stu_transcript_rollup in each row I want the distinct C_year_home_schools, and then I want 3 columns- one column for the total number of EPSOs that school offers for C_pathway_course = "Not a Pathway course", then grouping by student_id sum the total number of EPSOs each student attemps (d_creds_possible) at that school for C_pathway_course = "Not a Pathway course" and get the median by school, and then the last column is the same as above but d_creds_earn. So basically for each school, how many EPSOs do they offer that are not in pathways, and then what is the median number of EPSO credits attempted and earned by students at that school for non-pathway EPSOs.
epsos_not_in_pathways_by_school <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  
  # 1. All students by school (no EPSO filter yet)
  distinct(C_year_home_school, D_stu_id) %>%
  
  # 2. Bring in EPSO credits (non-pathway only)
  left_join(
    stu_transcript_rollup %>%
      filter(
        C_course_EPSO_no_IC == TRUE,
        C_pathway_course == "Not Pathway Course"
      ) %>%
      group_by(C_year_home_school, D_stu_id) %>%
      summarize(
        total_credits_attempted = sum(D_creds_possible, na.rm = TRUE),
        total_credits_earned    = sum(D_creds_earn, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = c("C_year_home_school", "D_stu_id")
  ) %>%
  
  # 3. Explicitly set non-attempters to zero
  mutate(
    total_credits_attempted = coalesce(total_credits_attempted, 0),
    total_credits_earned    = coalesce(total_credits_earned, 0)
  ) %>%
  
  # 4. Median by school (zeros included)
  group_by(C_year_home_school) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_credits_attempted = mean(total_credits_attempted),
    mean_credits_earned    = mean(total_credits_earned),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # 5. Add total EPSOs offered (school-level)
  left_join(
    stu_transcript_rollup %>%
      filter(
        C_course_EPSO_no_IC == TRUE,
        C_pathway_course == "Not Pathway Course"
      ) %>%
      group_by(C_year_home_school) %>%
      summarize(
        total_epsos_offered = n_distinct(C_course_name_clean),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "C_year_home_school"
  ) %>%
  
  arrange(C_year_home_school) %>%
  print()
```

```{r}
#Can we create a MECE bucket of number of students earning X number of world language credits total
world_language_credits_earned_buckets <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  filter(str_detect(C_course_subject_area, "World Language")) %>%
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    total_world_language_credits_earned = sum(D_creds_earn, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
 mutate(
  credits_earned_bucket = case_when(
    total_world_language_credits_earned == 0   ~ "0 credits",
    total_world_language_credits_earned == 0.5 ~ "0.5 credits",
    total_world_language_credits_earned == 1   ~ "1 credit",
    total_world_language_credits_earned == 1.5 ~ "1.5 credits",
    total_world_language_credits_earned == 2   ~ "2 credits",
    total_world_language_credits_earned == 2.5 ~ "2.5 credits",
    total_world_language_credits_earned >= 3 & total_world_language_credits_earned < 5 ~ "3–4.5 credits",
    total_world_language_credits_earned >= 5 & total_world_language_credits_earned < 7 ~ "5–6.5 credits",
    total_world_language_credits_earned >= 7 ~ "7+ credits"
  )
) %>%
  group_by(credits_earned_bucket) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(credits_earned_bucket) %>%
  print()

#Okay this might get a little tricky, but of the students who earned 2 or more credits in a world-language, how many of them did it in the SAME world language (like all "Spanish" or all "French") versus two different world languages (like "Spanish" and "French")
students_2plus_credits_single_vs_multiple_languages <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  # Keep only world language courses
  filter(str_detect(C_course_subject_area, "World Language")) %>%
  
  # Collapse course names into language families
  mutate(
    language_family = case_when(
      str_detect(C_course_name_clean, regex("spanish", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Spanish",
      str_detect(C_course_name_clean, regex("french", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "French",
      str_detect(C_course_name_clean, regex("japanese", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Japanese",
      str_detect(C_course_name_clean, regex("arabic", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Arabic",
      str_detect(C_course_name_clean, regex("german", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "German",
      str_detect(C_course_name_clean, regex("latin", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Latin",
      str_detect(C_course_name_clean, regex("sign", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "Sign Language",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  
  # Drop any WL courses that don't map cleanly to a language family
  filter(!is.na(language_family)) %>%
  
  # Sum credits within student x language
  group_by(D_stu_id, language_family) %>%
  summarize(
    credits_in_language = sum(D_creds_earn, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Compute total world language credits per student
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  mutate(
    total_wl_credits = sum(credits_in_language)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  # Keep only students with 2+ total WL credits
  filter(total_wl_credits >= 2) %>%
  
  # Determine whether credits came from one or multiple languages
  group_by(D_stu_id) %>%
  summarize(
    num_languages = n_distinct(language_family),
    single_vs_multiple = if_else(
      num_languages == 1,
      "Single Language",
      "Multiple Languages"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Final student counts
  group_by(single_vs_multiple) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

students_2plus_credits_single_vs_multiple_languages

  # Senior-year math only
  filter(
    C_eoy_grade == 12,
    C_course_subject_area == "Math"
  ) %>%
  # One row per student–course

  filter(n_distinct(C_course_id_clean) >= 2) %>%

  summarize(
    math_combo = paste(
      sort(unique(C_course_name_clean)),
      collapse = " + "
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Count students by combo
  group_by(math_combo) %>%
  summarize(
    num_students = n_distinct(D_stu_id),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Highest to lowest frequency
  arrange(desc(num_students))

#Trying this again
# ----------------------------
# 1. Build per-student math states using the lookup
# ----------------------------
math_by_grade <- stu_transcript_rollup %>%
  filter(C_course_subject_area == "Math") %>%
  # Join the lookup to get the common name
  left_join(math_courses_lookup, by = "C_course_name_clean") %>%
  # Use 'common_name' from the lookup for aggregation
  group_by(D_stu_id, C_eoy_grade) %>%
  summarise(
    math_state = paste(sort(unique(`Name Coded`)), collapse = " + "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ----------------------------
# 2. Pivot wide (one row per student)
# ----------------------------
math_wide <- math_by_grade %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = C_eoy_grade,
    values_from = math_state,
    names_prefix = "grade_"
  )

# ----------------------------
# 3. Helper function to build a clean Sankey table
# ----------------------------
build_transition_table <- function(df, from_grade, to_grade, min_n = 50) {
  
  raw_links <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[from_grade]]),
           !is.na(.data[[to_grade]])) %>%
    count(
      source = .data[[from_grade]],
      target = .data[[to_grade]],
      name = "n"
    )
  
  # Identify low-frequency TARGETS (within this transition only)
  small_targets <- raw_links %>%
    group_by(target) %>%
    summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(total < min_n) %>%
    pull(target)
  
  # Collapse them into "Other"
  cleaned <- raw_links %>%
    mutate(
      target = if_else(target %in% small_targets, "Other", target)
    ) %>%
    group_by(source, target) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(n))
  
  cleaned
}

# ----------------------------
# 4. Build tables for each grade transition
# ----------------------------
sankey_9_10  <- build_transition_table(math_wide, "grade_9",  "grade_10")
sankey_10_11 <- build_transition_table(math_wide, "grade_10", "grade_11")
sankey_11_12 <- build_transition_table(math_wide, "grade_11", "grade_12")
```
